chapter_title_en: The Warship and the Fried Dough
chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Chapter 385: The Warship and the Fried Dough — A Calm Voyage to Apricot Island
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang boards a fuchuan for Apricot Island, but the passage of a massive Great Liang warship and a child’s innocent laugh at his inner horror betray the calm.
og_title: A Warship Passes, and a Child Laughs at the Monster Within
og_description: On a calm sea voyage, Li Huowang feels the weight of a wider war and a little girl’s innocent delight in his body horror. The reunion with Zhuge Yuan looms.
twitter_title: The calmest chapter hides the sharpest knife.
twitter_description: Li Huowang sails toward Apricot Island, and even a child's playful curiosity feels like another kind of doom.

lore_anchors.definition: A traditional Chinese sailing vessel with a flat bottom, used for coastal and deep-sea voyages. In the Dao-Twisted World, it is a common passenger ship.
A historical Chinese card game, a precursor to mahjong, played with long, narrow cards. It was a popular gambling game during the Ming and Qing dynasties.
A method of preparing seafood by marinating it raw in a seasoned liquid. A coastal specialty of Huating City in this novel.
The name of Li Huowang’s yellow dog, who has been traveling with him since earlier chapters.
A small, round medicated plaster often applied to the temples or forehead for headaches; used to characterize the shady card player in this chapter.
The destination of the fuchuan, where Zhuge Yuan is presumably waiting. Its name evokes a pastoral, medicinal association.
A corrupted counterpart to the Heart-Element, capable of hiding or erasing concepts, objects, and memories from reality.
A grotesque parasitic entity residing inside Li Huowang, capable of independent movement. It has become a semi-domesticated part of his body horror.
A high-ranking eunuch official of the Supervisory Heavenly Office, who previously worked with Li Huowang on the Heart-Turbid search.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Li Huowang give a fake surname (Er) first?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He was testing the boat captain’s vigilance and also being a bit of a smartass, a common reflex for someone who has learned to distrust every interaction.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the significance of the Great Liang warship?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It shows the state is mobilizing massive martial resources for a mysterious overseas search, hinting at a larger cosmological or political threat beyond the personal horror Li Huowang faces.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did the Black Tai Sui snatch the little girl’s fried dough?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The Black Tai Sui is a parasite with its own budding intelligence and appetites. It acts on instinct, and Li Huowang’s lack of reaction shows how normalized the grotesque has become for him.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is the reunion with Zhuge Yuan going to be happy?
cultural_notes_faq.a: For Li Huowang, hope is always laced with suspicion. The book’s pattern suggests that any reunion, however welcome, will come with a steep price or a terrible revelation.
